task.name: A run with little review friction pads its knowledge summary with restatements of what shipped, so injection will spend its rendered-claim budget on prose that changes nothing
task.story_text:
## Observed

The knowledge corpus now holds 17 summaries in this repository and 2 in the `hdp`
adopter. Summaries produced by runs whose review loop surfaced real findings carry
transferable claims. Summaries produced by clean, low-friction runs pad
`what_was_learned` with restatements of the change itself.

From `.forge/knowledge/summaries/f7a4219a6d9e.yaml` (issue #2038, 1 review cycle,
approved clean):

> The project documents sandbox capability inputs in the user-facing inputs
> reference, indicating the extensible capability model is part of the supported
> configuration surface.

From `.forge/knowledge/summaries/e85a3864a258.yaml` (issue #2112):

> The plan-advisory measurement was implemented as a separate reporting surface,
> indicating this repository supports adding focused analytical tools without
> altering the main execution path.

The same pattern reproduces in the adopter repo — `hdp`'s summary for its issue
#335 (1 cycle, approved clean) claims "schema resource correctness depends on a
freshness gate", which is the change description restated. Its evidence entries
are circular: "This file was directly modified as the schema authority involved
in producing qualified table names" — the evidence says a file was modified, not
how the modification demonstrates the claim.

By contrast, `hdp`'s summary for its issue #337 — a run whose review raised two
P1s — carries claims that would genuinely redirect a future run (fail closed on
ambiguous identity mappings rather than picking a deterministic fallback;
regression guards must enumerate every exported user-data tool because review
caught one omitted).

Three facts make the padding costly rather than cosmetic:

- The validator already permits an empty `what_was_learned`
  (`knowledge_summary.py` accepts `proposed.get("what_was_learned") or []`;
  only non-empty entries must cite evidence). Padding is generation behavior,
  not a schema requirement.
- The renderer takes claims in artifact order and renders at most 5
  (`_MAX_RENDERED_CLAIMS` in `task/prior_run_selector.py`), truncating each
  field at 400 characters. Filler claims placed early displace stronger ones at
  the moment of injection.
- The selector offers at most 3 prior summaries per assembly, so in a small
  adopter corpus everything admissible gets injected and claim quality is the
  entire value proposition — there is no relevance scoring to filter a weak
  summary out.

## Expected

A persisted summary contains only claims that would change a future developer's
plan, implementation, or verification. A statement that merely says what
changed, where it changed, or that tests now exist is not a lesson and does not
appear as one.

A clean run with little to teach produces correspondingly few claims — or none —
rather than restatements manufactured to fill the section.

Claims are ordered strongest first, because only the first five are ever
rendered into a later run's context.

Every evidence description explains how the cited finding, cycle, file, or diff
demonstrates the claim, not merely that a file was part of the change.

## Diagnosis

**Baseline:** `d0d03c05abdc6f7cd01a7bc2ad09e75891a5a4e3` captured at `2026-08-20T06:54:34.863819+00:00`

**Inspected files:**

- `src/theforge/task/summary_prompts.py` — `sha256:637c5b680835bc8e9778d4f29872cfa892121e6751591334550443da66f80380`
- `src/theforge/coordinator/knowledge_summary_flow.py` — `sha256:ced51015f310c289c1ec51be5eb12a819a1cdff980a0ed9587ecec78bb38a423`
- `src/theforge/knowledge_summary.py` — `sha256:ee958a8d065137b01e527f92f42a271a88b28871b5d9ee5f67ee9948361273d0`
- `src/theforge/task/prior_run_selector.py` — `sha256:11524de39b866a934c9ffa15482f2e89cbc79a054a293783510334e414e4a33d`
- `.forge/knowledge/summaries/f7a4219a6d9e.yaml` — `sha256:73ed9523b9d10ee4f2ae875f2194d3d14c6a2f17566986c61341aed62ba05722`
- `.forge/knowledge/summaries/e85a3864a258.yaml` — `sha256:d83accbd32f60ff7069fad54e00ff1f094508c9edbf683b9b39f70c04edb2ec2`

### Observed symptom

Knowledge summaries produced by clean, low-friction runs (few or zero review
findings) pad `what_was_learned` with claims that merely restate what the run
changed ("X was implemented as Y, indicating the repo supports Z") rather than
claims that would redirect a future run's plan, implementation, or
verification. These filler claims are indistinguishable in shape from real
lessons, so the injection pipeline treats them as equally valuable — and
since claims are rendered in artifact order with no strength ordering, filler
placed early can displace stronger claims that never make it into the
rendered budget.

### Reproduction / evidence

.forge/knowledge/summaries/f7a4219a6d9e.yaml (issue #2038, 1 review cycle,
approved clean) — 5 what_was_learned entries, several of which are
restatements: "The project documents sandbox capability inputs in the
user-facing inputs reference, indicating the extensible capability model is
part of the supported configuration surface" and "The run established
regression coverage for config parsing..." — both just describe what was
done/where, not a transferable lesson.

.forge/knowledge/summaries/e85a3864a258.yaml (issue #2112) — "The
plan-advisory measurement was implemented as a separate reporting surface,
indicating this repository supports adding focused analytical tools without
altering the main execution path" is the change description restated as an
"indicating" claim.

By contrast, hdp's issue #337 summary (2 P1 findings surfaced in review)
carries claims that would actually redirect behavior (fail closed on
ambiguous identity mappings; regression guards must enumerate every exported
user-data tool).

### Hypotheses tested

- **[ruled out]** The validator (knowledge_summary.py:validate_proposed_summary) requires a minimum number of what_was_learned entries or otherwise forces non-empty output, so generation pads to satisfy a floor.
  - Evidence: validate_proposed_summary reads `proposed.get('what_was_learned') or []` (knowledge_summary.py:336) and applies no minimum-count check — only a max cap (_MAX_CLAIMS=20, line 341-345). An empty list passes validation cleanly. There is no schema pressure to produce any claims at all, let alone restatement filler.
- **[ruled out]** The renderer (prior_run_selector.py) or admissibility/selection logic scores or filters claims for quality, so a weak claim surviving there is a renderer bug, not a generation bug.
  - Evidence: _evidenced_claims/_dev_grounded_claims in prior_run_selector.py (lines 583-622) only filter for having valid evidence citations and truncate to claims[:_MAX_RENDERED_CLAIMS] (=5) in *artifact order* — there is no relevance/quality scoring anywhere in the selection or render path. This is a pass-through, confirming the issue's own description that quality is entirely a generation-time property.
- **[confirmed]** The summary-generation prompt (task/summary_prompts.py:build_run_summary_prompt) gives the model no instruction to omit restatement claims, no instruction that empty/short what_was_learned is an acceptable or expected outcome for a clean run, no instruction to order claims strongest-first, and no instruction that evidence descriptions must explain *how* the citation demonstrates the claim rather than merely that a file/finding/cycle was involved — so a low-friction run with nothing substantive to report still produces a full list of plausible-sounding filler to fill the section.
  - Evidence: Read the full prompt template (summary_prompts.py:131-200). The output
skeleton example itself models one `what_was_learned` entry with an evidence
block whose description says "Why this reference supports the claim" — the
only line steering claim/evidence quality is "A broad claim you cannot cite
is worse than no claim. Omit it," which is a citability instruction (can you
attach a resolvable reference?), not a substantiveness instruction (is this a
lesson at all, versus a restatement of the change?). Nothing in the prompt:
(a) defines what disqualifies a claim as "not a lesson" (restating what/where
changed, or that tests now exist), (b) tells the model a clean run can and
should emit few or zero claims, (c) asks for strongest-first ordering (which
matters because the renderer truncates to 5 in artifact order — confirmed
above), or (d) requires evidence descriptions to explain the causal link
between the citation and the claim rather than just restate involvement. The
observed summaries' filler claims ("indicating X supports Y", "the run
established regression coverage for...") are exactly the shape you'd expect
an instruction-following model to produce when told to fill a
`what_was_learned:` section with N reusable lessons and given no permission
or criterion to leave it short.

### Confirmed cause

The knowledge-summary generation prompt in
src/theforge/task/summary_prompts.py (build_run_summary_prompt) does not
instruct the model on what disqualifies a claim as a non-lesson (a
restatement of what/where something changed, or that tests now exist), does
not tell it that a clean/low-friction run may and should produce a short or
empty what_was_learned list, does not ask for claims to be ordered
strongest-first, and does not require evidence descriptions to explain the
causal mechanism (how the cited finding/cycle/file/diff demonstrates the
claim) rather than merely naming that it was involved. Because the schema
layer (knowledge_summary.py) imposes no minimum-count floor and the renderer
(prior_run_selector.py) applies no quality/relevance scoring — both
confirmed by code inspection — claim quality is entirely a function of what
the generation prompt asks for, and the prompt currently asks for neither
substantiveness nor ordering.

### Affected code path

src/theforge/task/summary_prompts.py:118-200 (build_run_summary_prompt) —
specifically the "Evidence rules" section (158-175) and the
`what_was_learned` / evidence-item guidance in the output skeleton
(188-193).

### Fix-success criterion

Regenerating a summary for a clean, low-review-friction run (e.g. re-running
the prompt against the same audit record as f7a4219a6d9e or e85a3864a258)
produces a what_was_learned list that is shorter (including possibly empty)
and contains no entries whose claim is a restatement of what/where the
change happened or that tests/coverage now exist; any surviving evidence
descriptions explain the causal link between the citation and the claim
rather than only naming the file/finding/cycle involved; and when a summary
has more than 5 claims, the strongest (most transferable) ones are ordered
first so the renderer's 5-claim truncation does not drop them.

### Related findings (out of scope)

> These are adjacent problems noticed during investigation. They are **not** the cause of this issue's symptom and are **out of scope for this fix** — triage them separately under the linked issue. Do not implement them as part of this issue.

- hdp adopter summary for issue #335 has circular evidence descriptions ('This file was directly modified as the schema authority involved in producing qualified table names') — same root cause as this issue (prompt gives no mechanism-explanation requirement), but that repo is outside this repo's fix scope; the fix here should transfer to it once shipped.
- _render_anchor_catalogue in summary_prompts.py truncates the file-path anchor listing to _MAX_FILES (60) sorted entries without indicating truncation to the model — not related to this issue's symptom, but a separate latent completeness gap if a run touches more than 60 files.

### Notes

This diagnosis is generation-prompt-scoped per the issue's own framing
(validator already permits empty what_was_learned; renderer already takes
claims in artifact order with a 5-claim cap; selector already offers at most
3 summaries). No code path outside the prompt needs to change to fix the
stated symptom. I did not attempt to reproduce by actually invoking the
summary agent (would cost real API spend); the diagnosis rests on reading
the prompt template against the two cited on-disk summaries, which is
sufficient to show the prompt lacks any substantiveness/ordering/mechanism
instruction that would explain why they differ from the #337-style summary.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
